page: Microsoft Azure E248ds_v7 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel processor and managed through Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 248 dedicated vCPUs paired with 1,888.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a memory density of 7.61 GB per vCPU. Hardware resources also feature 15,120 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, along with compatibility for Azure Premium Storage. The instance does not include GPU accelerators.

The compute environment is characterized by dedicated core scheduling, mitigating multi-tenant interference across its 248 virtual processors. By incorporating more than 15 TB of direct-attached NVMe disk alongside roughly 1.8 TB of system memory, the instance avoids network-attached storage latency bottlenecks for temporary data structures, write-ahead logs, and staging tables. The hardware profile balances extensive compute scaling with high I/O throughput capabilities.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the consolidation of extreme memory capacity and extensive local NVMe flash reduces the need to maintain distributed node clusters for large working sets. Microsoft Azure E248ds_v7 is tailored for memory-bound, I/O-intensive enterprise workloads, including large-scale relational database engines, in-memory analytical databases, extensive caching layers, and high-volume transaction processing systems.
description: Microsoft Azure E248ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on Microsoft Hyper-V with an x86_64 Intel processor architecture. Configured with 248 dedicated vCPUs and 1,888.0 GB of RAM, the instance delivers approximately 7.61 GB of memory per core. A key hardware component is its 15,120 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, providing substantial fast transient storage alongside Premium Storage capabilities. The instance lacks dedicated GPU accelerators, focusing strictly on high-density CPU and RAM workloads. By coupling massive system memory with high-capacity local NVMe drives, the E248ds_v7 provides strong resource efficiency for memory-bound systems avoiding external storage latencies. It is suitable for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise relational database management systems, real-time big data processing pipelines, and intensive transactional applications demanding significant memory capacity and fast scratch storage.
